title: The Sixth Day
body:
In the morning the Lord rides the Hanumantha Vāhanam, representing Hanumān, the very embodiment of devotion and service. Hanumān's dedication to Sri Rāma reminds every devotee of the value of loyalty and selfless service.

In the evening comes the Swarṇa Rathōtsavam, in which the Lord is drawn in procession on a golden chariot, intricately decorated, signifying prosperity and divine majesty, and drawing great crowds of devotees.

At night the Lord rides the Gaja Vāhanam, the elephant, a symbol of royalty and abundance, associated with the Lord's power to remove obstacles and bestow good fortune.
